title: Ezekiel 43:18 – Ezekiel 43:27
paragraphs: Record type: Temple vision and ordinances. Source section: The Ordinances of the Altar.

Ezekiel 43:19 — You will give the Levitical priests who are of Zadok’s offspring and draw near to Me to minister to Me, says the Lord God, a calf from the cattle as an offering for sin.
Ezekiel 43:20 — They will take some of its blood and put it on the altar’s four horns, on the four corners of the place of atonement, and on the base all around. They will make atonement for it.
Ezekiel 43:21 — They will take the calf for the sin offering, and it will be burned in the separated area of the house, outside the holy places.
Ezekiel 43:22 — On the second day they will take two unblemished goat kids for sin, and they will make atonement for the altar as they made atonement with the calf.
Ezekiel 43:23 — After you have completed the atonement, they will bring an unblemished calf from the cattle and an unblemished ram from the sheep.
Ezekiel 43:24 — You all will bring them before the Lord, and the priests will throw salt upon them and offer them as burnt offerings to the Lord.
Ezekiel 43:25 — For seven days you will prepare a kid for sin each day, and a calf from the cattle and a ram from the sheep. They will prepare unblemished animals—
Ezekiel 43:26 — —for seven days. They will make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and they will fill their hands.
Ezekiel 43:27 — From the eighth day onward, the priests will offer your burnt offerings and your offerings for well-being on the altar. I will accept you, says the Lord.”

title: Ezekiel 46:1 – Ezekiel 46:13
paragraphs: Record type: Temple vision and ordinances. Source section: The Gate of the Inner Court on the Sabbath.

Ezekiel 46:1 — “Thus says the Lord God: The gate in the inner court facing east will be shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.

Ezekiel 46:2 — The ruler will enter by the porch of the outer gate and stand at the gate’s vestibules. The priests will offer his burnt offerings and his offerings for well-being. He will bow down at the gate’s vestibule and go out, and the gate will certainly not be shut until evening.
Ezekiel 46:3 — The people of the land will bow down before the Lord at the vestibules of that gate on Sabbaths and new moons.
Ezekiel 46:4 — The ruler will present burnt offerings to the Lord: on the Sabbath day, six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram,
Ezekiel 46:5 — with a grain offering of a cake for the ram, and for the lambs an offering as the gift of his hand, with a hin of oil for each cake.
Ezekiel 46:6 — On the day of the new moon there will be an unblemished calf and six lambs, and the ram will be unblemished.
Ezekiel 46:7 — A cake for the ram and a cake for the calf will be the grain offering, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.
Ezekiel 46:8 — When the ruler enters, he will enter by the porch of the gate and go out by the way of the gate.

Ezekiel 46:9 — When the people of the land come before the Lord at the festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to bow down will go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate will go out by the north gate. He will not return through the gate by which he entered, but will go out straight opposite it.
Ezekiel 46:10 — The ruler will be among them: when they enter, he will enter with them, and when they go out, he will go out.

Ezekiel 46:11 — At the festivals and public assemblies the grain offering will be a cake for each calf, a cake for each ram, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

Ezekiel 46:12 — If the ruler makes a pledged offering, a burnt offering for well-being to the Lord, he will open for himself the gate facing east and offer his burnt offering and his offerings for well-being as he does on the Sabbath day. He will go out and close the doors after he has gone out.
Ezekiel 46:13 — He will prepare an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the Lord; in the morning he will prepare it.

Context and scope: These ordinances belong to Ezekiel’s temple-and-land vision. The record preserves the text without deciding between competing accounts of its fulfillment or imposing the ancient offices and sacrifices on all believers.

verses.text: “Thus says the Lord God: The gate in the inner court facing east will be shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.

The ruler will enter by the porch of the outer gate and stand at the gate’s vestibules. The priests will offer his burnt offerings and his offerings for well-being. He will bow down at the gate’s vestibule and go out, and the gate will certainly not be shut until evening.
The people of the land will bow down before the Lord at the vestibules of that gate on Sabbaths and new moons.
The ruler will present burnt offerings to the Lord: on the Sabbath day, six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram,
with a grain offering of a cake for the ram, and for the lambs an offering as the gift of his hand, with a hin of oil for each cake.
On the day of the new moon there will be an unblemished calf and six lambs, and the ram will be unblemished.
A cake for the ram and a cake for the calf will be the grain offering, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.
When the ruler enters, he will enter by the porch of the gate and go out by the way of the gate.

When the people of the land come before the Lord at the festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to bow down will go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate will go out by the north gate. He will not return through the gate by which he entered, but will go out straight opposite it.
The ruler will be among them: when they enter, he will enter with them, and when they go out, he will go out.
At the festivals and public assemblies the grain offering will be a cake for each calf, a cake for each ram, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

If the ruler makes a pledged offering, a burnt offering for well-being to the Lord, he will open for himself the gate facing east and offer his burnt offering and his offerings for well-being as he does on the Sabbath day. He will go out and close the doors after he has gone out.
He will prepare an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the Lord; in the morning he will prepare it.

title: Not to suppose that He came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; to do and teach even the least of these commandments, with a righteousness greater than that of the scribes and Pharisees.
paragraphs: Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to abolish, but to fulfil. For truly I tell you: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota nor one stroke shall pass from the Law, until all things come to pass. Whoever therefore loosens one of these least commandments and teaches people to do so shall be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches them shall be called great in the kingdom of the heavens. title: Murder: whoever is angry with his brother, insults him or calls him a fool is liable to judgment.
category: You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You
paragraphs: You have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not murder’; and ‘whoever murders shall be liable to judgment.’ But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ shall be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool,’ shall be liable to the Gehenna of fire.

title: To be reconciled with your brother before you bring your gift to the altar, and to come to terms quickly with your accuser.
category: You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You
paragraphs: If therefore you offer your gift upon the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift. Come to terms with your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the way, lest your adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.

title: Adultery: whoever looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery in his heart; better to lose an eye or a hand than to be thrown into Gehenna.
category: You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You
paragraphs: You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall not commit adultery.’ But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart. If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna. And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go into Gehenna.

title: Oaths: not to swear at all; let your word be Yes, yes, or No, no.
category: You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You
paragraphs: Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not swear falsely, but shall fulfil your oaths to the Lord.’ But I tell you: do not swear at all, neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God, nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of His feet, nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King. Nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black. But let your word be ‘Yes, yes’; ‘No, no.’ Whatever is beyond these is of evil.

title: An eye for an eye: not to resist the evil person; to turn the other cheek, give the cloak also, go the second mile, and give to the one who asks.
category: You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You
paragraphs: You have heard that it was said: ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I tell you: do not resist the evildoer; but whoever strikes you upon your right cheek, turn the other to him also. And if anyone would sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak also. And whoever compels you to go one Roman mile, go with him two. Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who would borrow from you.

title: Love of neighbor: to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so as to be sons of your Father in the heavens; to be perfect as He is perfect.
category: You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You
paragraphs: You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’ But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you, that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens; for He makes His sun rise upon the evil and the good, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing beyond others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You shall therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
See also: Luke 6:27–28 · Luke 6:32–36 In the Law: 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

title: What God has yoked together, no human being is to separate. Moses permitted divorce because of hardness of heart, but from the beginning it was not so.
paragraphs: He answered, “Have you not read that the Creator from the beginning made them male and female, and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’? So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has yoked together, let no human being separate.” They said to Him, “Why then did Moses command giving a certificate of divorce and divorcing her?” He said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart Moses permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so. I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery.”

paragraphs: He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him: how he entered God’s house in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of presentation, which only priests may lawfully eat, and also gave them to those who were with him?” And He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath. Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand. There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.” When He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable. He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him, because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods. He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person. For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders, adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness. All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”

paragraphs: Enter through the narrow gate, because the gate is wide and the road broad that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. How narrow is the gate and how constricted the road that leads to life, and few find it!

title: To deny yourself, take up your cross, and follow Him.
paragraphs: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “If anyone wishes to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life because of Me will find it.
See also: Mark 8:34–35 · Luke 9:23–24 · Matthew 10:38–39

title: To come to Him, take His yoke, and learn from Him.
paragraphs: Come to Me, all you who labour and are burdened, and I will give you rest. Take My yoke upon you, and learn from Me; for I am meek and lowly in heart, and you shall find rest for your souls. For My yoke is easy, and My burden is light.”

title: To let the dead bury their own dead, and not to look back from the plow.
paragraphs: He said to him, “Let the dead bury their own dead; but you go and proclaim God’s kingdom.” Another also said, “I will follow Thee, Lord; but first permit me to say farewell to those in my house.” Jesus said to him, “No one who puts his hand to a plow and looks backward is fit for God’s kingdom.”
See also: Matthew 8:22

title: To count the cost: whoever does not renounce all that he has cannot be His disciple.
paragraphs: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be My disciple. Whoever does not carry his own cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple. For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the expense, whether he has enough to finish it? Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and is unable to complete it, all who see it may begin to mock him, saying, ‘This man began to build and was unable to finish.’ Or what king, going to meet another king in war, will not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand? And if not, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace. So, therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all his own possessions cannot be My disciple.
See also: Matthew 10:37

title: To hear His words and do them, like the man who built upon the rock.
paragraphs: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and puts them into practice will be likened to a prudent man who built his house upon the rock. The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and fell upon that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock. And everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not put them into practice will be likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand. The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell; and its fall was great.”
See also: Luke 6:46–49

title: To remain in Him and in His love.
paragraphs: Remain in Me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit from itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you unless you remain in Me. I am the vine; you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit, because apart from Me you can do nothing.
See also: John 15:9

paragraphs: Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that remains for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for upon Him the Father, God, has set His seal.”

verses.text: Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that remains for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for upon Him the Father, God, has set His seal.”

paragraphs: So let your light shine before people, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in the heavens.

verses.text: So let your light shine before people, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in the heavens.

title: A new commandment: to love one another as He has loved you.
paragraphs: I give you a new commandment: that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another. By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you have love among one another.”
See also: John 15:12 · John 15:17 In the Law: 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

paragraphs: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

verses.text: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

title: To love your enemies, do good, and lend expecting nothing back.
paragraphs: But love your enemies, do good, and lend, expecting nothing back. Your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because He is kind to the ungrateful and evil.
See also: Matthew 5:44 In the Law: 36. Lending without exploiting the needy

title: Go, and do likewise: to show mercy as the Samaritan did.
paragraphs: Which of these three seems to you to have become a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?” He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go, and you do likewise.”
In the Law: 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

title: Not to judge, so that you are not judged; first to take the beam out of your own eye.
paragraphs: Do not judge, so that you may not be judged. For with the judgment you use, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you. Why do you see the splinter in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the beam in your own eye? Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Let me remove the splinter from your eye,’ when behold, the beam is in your own eye? Hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the splinter from your brother’s eye.
See also: Luke 6:37–38 · Luke 6:41–42

title: To forgive, so that your Father may forgive you.
paragraphs: For if you forgive people their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you do not forgive people, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
See also: Mark 11:25 · Luke 6:37 In the Law: 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

title: To forgive your brother not seven times but seventy times seven.
paragraphs: Then Peter came and said to Him, “Lord, how often will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?” Jesus says to him, “I tell you, not up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.
See also: Luke 17:3–4 In the Law: 78. Correcting a neighbor responsibly · 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

title: If your brother sins, to show him his fault between you and him alone; then with one or two others; then to tell it to the church.
paragraphs: If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother. But if he does not hear, take one or two more with you, so that every matter may be established upon the mouth of two or three witnesses. If he refuses to hear them, tell the Church. And if he refuses to hear even the Church, let him be to you like the Gentile and the tax collector.
In the Law: 78. Correcting a neighbor responsibly · 137. Corroborated testimony in serious cases

paragraphs: It shall not be so among you. Instead, whoever wishes to become great among you will be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you will be your slave, just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give His life as a ransom in place of many.”

paragraphs: So if I, the Lord and the Teacher, washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, so that you also may do just as I did to you.

paragraphs: But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will have honor before all who recline at table with you. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

paragraphs: But you shall not be called ‘Rabbi,’ for One is your Teacher, and you are all brothers. And call no one upon earth your father, for One is your Father, the heavenly One. Nor shall you be called guides, because One is your Guide, the Christ.

title: When you give a feast, to invite the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind.
category: The Little Ones and the Poor
paragraphs: He also said to the one who had invited Him, “When you give a midday meal or a supper, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and you receive repayment. But when you give a reception, invite the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind. And you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”

title: To give alms in secret.
paragraphs: Take care not to practice your righteousness before people in order to be seen by them; otherwise you have no reward with your Father in the heavens. So when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and streets, so that people may glorify them. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full. But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing, so that your almsgiving may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.

title: To pray in secret, and not to babble as the nations do.
paragraphs: And when you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites, because they love to pray standing in synagogues and at street corners, so that people may see them. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full. But you, when you pray, enter your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you. When praying, do not babble like the Gentiles, for they think they will be heard through their many words. So do not become like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.

paragraphs: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.

And will He delay over them? I tell you, He will bring about justice for them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on the earth?”

paragraphs: And on that day you will ask Me nothing. Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask the Father anything, He will give it to you in My name. Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be made full.

paragraphs: Jesus answered them, “Have faith in God. Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says is happening, it will be his. Therefore I tell you, everything you pray and ask for—believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.

verses.text: He said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Therefore petition the Lord of the harvest to send workers out into His harvest.

verses.text: Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

title: Not to store up treasures on earth, but in heaven.
paragraphs: Do not store up treasures for yourselves upon earth, where moth and consumption destroy and where thieves break through and steal. But store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor consumption destroys and where thieves neither break through nor steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart will also be.
See also: Luke 12:33–34

paragraphs: No one can serve as a slave to two masters: for he will either hate the one and love the other, or hold to one and despise the other. You cannot serve as a slave to God and mammon.

paragraphs: And I tell you, make friends for yourselves from the mammon of unrighteousness, so that when it fails, they may welcome you into the eternal tents. The one who is faithful in the least is faithful also in much, and the one who is unrighteous in the least is unrighteous also in much.

Is life not more than food, and the body more than clothing? Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow or reap or gather into storehouses, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they?

title: To stay awake, for you do not know the day or the hour.
paragraphs: Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour.
See also: Matthew 24:42–44 · Mark 13:33–37 · Luke 12:35–40

verses.text: Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour.

title: To watch yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down, and to stay awake at all times, praying.
paragraphs: But watch yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with carousing and drunkenness and the cares of life, and that day come upon you suddenly like a trap. For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth. But stay awake at every season, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.”

title: To beware of false prophets, who come in sheep’s clothing.
paragraphs: Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves. You will recognize them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
See also: Matthew 24:4–5 · Mark 13:5–6 · Luke 21:8 In the Law: 125. Rejecting a prophet who leads to other gods

title: To beware of the leaven of the Pharisees.
paragraphs: Jesus said to them, “Look out and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
See also: Mark 8:15 · Luke 12:1

verses.text: Jesus said to them, “Look out and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

title: Not to give what is holy to dogs or cast your pearls before swine.
paragraphs: Do not give what is holy to dogs or throw your pearls before pigs, lest they trample them with their feet and turn and tear you apart.

verses.text: Do not give what is holy to dogs or throw your pearls before pigs, lest they trample them with their feet and turn and tear you apart.

title: To be prudent as snakes and innocent as doves.
paragraphs: Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves. So become prudent as snakes and innocent as doves.

verses.text: Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves. So become prudent as snakes and innocent as doves.

title: To remember Lot’s wife.
paragraphs: Remember Lot’s wife. Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses it will keep it alive.

verses.text: Remember Lot’s wife. Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses it will keep it alive.

title: To acknowledge Him before people.
paragraphs: Therefore everyone who acknowledges Me before people, I too will acknowledge before My Father in the heavens. But whoever denies Me before people, I too will deny before My Father in the heavens.

title: Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in yourselves.
category: Do This in Remembrance of Me
paragraphs: So Jesus said to them, “Amen, amen, I tell you: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in yourselves. The one who eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day. For My flesh is true food, and My blood is true drink. The one who eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.

title: To go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to observe everything He commanded.
paragraphs: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority in heaven and upon earth has been given to Me. Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to keep all that I commanded you; and behold, I am with you all the days, until the consummation of the age.”
See also: Mark 16:15–16
Textual note: The parallel Mark 16:15–16 is part of Mark’s longer ending; see the linked chapter’s textual notes.

title: That repentance and forgiveness of sins be proclaimed in His name to all the nations; to remain in the city until clothed with power from on high.
paragraphs: and said to them, “Thus it is written that the Christ should suffer and rise from the dead on the third day, and that repentance for the forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in His name to all the nations—beginning from Jerusalem. You are witnesses of these things. And behold, I am sending out the promise of My Father upon you; but remain in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.”
See also: Acts 1:4–5 · Acts 1:8

title: As the Father has sent Me, I also send you. Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you forgive are forgiven.
paragraphs: Then Jesus said to them again, “Peace to you. Just as the Father has sent Me, I also send you.” And having said this, He breathed and says to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they have been forgiven them; if you retain those of any, they have been retained.”

title: To proclaim that the kingdom has drawn near, to heal the sick; freely you received, freely give.
paragraphs: As you go, proclaim, ‘The kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.’ Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Freely you received; freely give.
See also: Luke 9:2 · Luke 10:9

title: To take nothing for the road, to remain in one house, and to shake off the dust where you are not received.
paragraphs: He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff alone: no bread, no bag, no copper money in their belt, but to wear sandals, and, “Do not put on two tunics.” He said to them, “Wherever you enter a house, remain there until you leave that place. Whatever place does not receive you, and whose people do not listen to you, shake off the dust beneath your feet as you leave there, as a testimony to them.”
See also: Matthew 10:9–14 · Luke 9:3–5 · Luke 10:4–11

title: When they hand you over, not to be anxious how or what you will speak.
paragraphs: When they hand you over, do not be anxious about how or what you should speak, for what you should speak will be given to you at that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
See also: Mark 13:11 · Luke 12:11–12 · Luke 21:14–15

title: When they persecute you in one city, to flee to the next.
paragraphs: When they persecute you in this city, flee to the other. For truly I tell you, you will certainly not finish going through the cities of Israel until the Son of Man comes.

verses.text: When they persecute you in this city, flee to the other. For truly I tell you, you will certainly not finish going through the cities of Israel until the Son of Man comes.

title: To rejoice and be glad when you are reviled and persecuted for His sake.
paragraphs: Blessed are you when they revile you and persecute you and falsely speak every evil thing against you for My sake. Rejoice and be glad, for great is your reward in the heavens; for thus they persecuted the prophets before you.
See also: Luke 6:22–23

paragraphs: Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names have been written in the heavens.”

title: Not to stop the one who does a mighty work in His name: whoever is not against us is for us.

title: To feed His lambs and shepherd His sheep.
paragraphs: So when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus says to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me more than these?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, Thou knowest that I love Thee.” He says to him, “Feed My lambs.” He says to him again a second time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, Thou knowest that I love Thee.” He says to him, “Shepherd My sheep.” He says to him the third time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” Peter was grieved because He said to him the third time, “Do you love Me?” And he said to Him, “Lord, Thou knowest all things; Thou knowest that I love Thee.” Jesus says to him, “Feed My sheep.

title: To owe no one anything except to love one another: the commandments are summed up in this word, You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
category: Love, the Fulfilling of the Law
paragraphs: Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law. For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” Love does not work evil toward the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.

title: By this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments and walk as He walked.
category: Love, the Fulfilling of the Law
paragraphs: And by this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments. The one who says, “I have come to know Him,” and does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in that person. But whoever keeps His word, in that person the love of God has truly been brought to completion. By this we know that we are in Him. The one who says that he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked.

title: To bless those who persecute you; to repay no one evil for evil; to overcome evil with good.

If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people. Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.” But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head. title: Blessing and cursing come out of the same mouth; this ought not to be. Can a fig tree bear olives?.
paragraphs: With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings who have been made in God’s likeness. From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to happen this way. Does a spring pour out sweet and bitter water from the same opening? My brothers, can a fig tree produce olives, or a vine figs? title: Godliness with contentment is great gain; the love of money is a root of all evils.

But those who want to become rich fall into temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge human beings into ruin and destruction. For the love of money is a root of all evils, and some, reaching for it, wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains.

title: Come now, you rich: your gold and silver have rusted; the wages you withheld from the workers cry out.
paragraphs: Come now, you rich people: weep and howl over the miseries coming upon you. Your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten. Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be a testimony against you and will devour your flesh. You have stored up treasure like fire in the last days. Look, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, withheld by you, cry out; and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of the Lord Sabaoth. You lived luxuriously on the earth and indulged yourselves; you fattened your hearts on a day of slaughter.

title: I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.
paragraphs: For through law I died to law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ. And I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me.
Also taught in: Galatians 5:24 · Galatians 6:14 The word of Christ: To deny yourself, take up your cross, and follow Him

title: To rejoice insofar as you share Christ’s sufferings; if you are reviled for the name of Christ, you are blessed.
paragraphs: Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal among you, which comes upon you for testing, as though something strange were happening to you. But insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that you may also rejoice with exultation at the revelation of His glory. If you are reviled for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you.
Also taught in: Acts 5:41 The word of Christ: To rejoice and be glad when you are reviled and persecuted for His sake

title: To count it all joy when you fall into various trials, for the testing of your faith produces endurance.
paragraphs: Count it all joy, my brothers, whenever you encounter trials of various kinds, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. And let endurance have its complete work, so that you may be complete and whole, lacking in nothing.
Also taught in: Romans 5:3–5 The word of Christ: To rejoice and be glad when you are reviled and persecuted for His sake

title: If we endure, we shall also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He also will deny us.
paragraphs: The saying is faithful: for if we died with Him, we will also live with Him; if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He also will deny us; if we are unfaithful, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.
The word of Christ: To acknowledge Him before people

title: The day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night; so let us not sleep as the rest do, but stay awake and be sober.
category: Watchfulness and the Day of the Lord
paragraphs: Now concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need for anything to be written to you. For you yourselves know precisely that the day of the Lord comes in this way, like a thief in the night. When they say, “Peace and security,” then sudden destruction comes upon them, as labor pain upon a pregnant woman, and they will certainly not escape. But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day should overtake you like a thief. For you are all sons of light and sons of day. We are not of night or darkness. So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us keep watch and be sober.
The word of Christ: To stay awake, for you do not know the day or the hour · To watch yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down, and to stay awake at all times…

title: To be sober and watchful: your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion.
category: Watchfulness and the Day of the Lord
paragraphs: Be sober; be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks about like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. Resist him, firm in the faith, knowing that the same kinds of sufferings are being experienced by your brotherhood in the world.
The word of Christ: To keep watch and pray that you may not enter temptation

title: The day of the Lord will come like a thief; what sort of people ought you to be, in holy conduct and godliness.
category: Watchfulness and the Day of the Lord
paragraphs: But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a rushing roar, and the elements will be dissolved by burning heat, and the earth and the works in it will be found. Since all these things are being dissolved in this way, what sort of people ought you to be in holy acts of conduct and godliness, waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be dissolved by fire and the elements melt in burning heat?
The word of Christ: To stay awake, for you do not know the day or the hour

title: To be patient until the coming of the Lord; the Judge is standing at the doors.
category: Watchfulness and the Day of the Lord
paragraphs: Be patient, therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Look, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it until he receives the early and late rain. You too be patient; strengthen your hearts, because the coming of the Lord has drawn near. Do not groan against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Look, the Judge stands before the doors.
The word of Christ: To stay awake, for you do not know the day or the hour

title: Not to believe every spirit, but to test the spirits, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
category: Watchfulness and the Day of the Lord
paragraphs: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ as having come in the flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. And this is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and is already in the world now.
Also taught in: 2 Peter 2:1 The word of Christ: To beware of false prophets, who come in sheep’s clothing

title: Savage wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock; therefore be alert.
category: Watchfulness and the Day of the Lord
paragraphs: I know that after my departure fierce wolves will enter among you, not sparing the flock. Even from among you yourselves men will arise, speaking distorted things to draw the disciples away after themselves. Therefore stay awake, remembering that for three years, night and day, I never ceased admonishing each one with tears.

paragraphs: Therefore I urge you, brothers, through God’s mercies, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, your rational worship. And do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of the mind, so that you may discern what God’s will is: the good and pleasing and perfect.
The word of Christ: The hour is coming when the Father will be worshiped neither on this mountain nor in…

title: You are God’s temple, and the Spirit of God dwells among you.
paragraphs: Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells among you? If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy that person. For God’s temple is holy, and that is what you are.

title: Not to love the world or the things in the world.
paragraphs: Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For everything in the world—the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the boastfulness of life—is not from the Father, but is from the world. And the world is passing away, and its desire; but the one who does the will of God abides forever.

title: Pure and undefiled religion: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained from the world.

title: To let brotherly love continue, not to neglect hospitality, and to remember the prisoners as though in prison with them.
paragraphs: Let brotherly love remain. Do not forget hospitality, for through it some unknowingly entertained angels. Remember the prisoners as fellow prisoners, and those being mistreated, as you yourselves also are in a body.

title: Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
paragraphs: What, then, shall we say Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found? For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast of—but not before God. For what does the Scripture say? “And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.” Now to the one who works, the wage is not reckoned according to grace, but according to what is owed. But to the one who does not work, but believes in the One who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness,
Also taught in: Galatians 3:6–7 · James 2:23 Scripture and event: Abraham believes the promise, Genesis 15:6

title: Abraham was shown righteous by works when he offered Isaac on the altar: faith was working together with his works.
paragraphs: Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered Isaac his son upon the altar? You see that faith was working together with his works, and by the works faith was brought to completion, and the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God. You see that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone.
Also taught in: Hebrews 11:17–19 Scripture and event: The binding of Isaac, Genesis 22:9–12

title: By faith Abel offered, Enoch was taken, and Noah built the ark.
paragraphs: By faith Abel offered God a greater sacrifice than Cain, through which he received testimony that he was righteous, God testifying concerning his gifts; and through it, though he died, he still speaks. By faith Enoch was taken away so as not to see death, and he was not found, because God took him away. For before his taking away he had received testimony that he had pleased God. And without faith it is impossible to please Him, for the one approaching God must believe that He is and that He becomes a rewarder of those who seek Him. By faith Noah, instructed concerning things not yet seen, acted with reverent fear and prepared an ark for the salvation of his household. Through this he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness according to faith.
Scripture and event: Abel’s offering, Genesis 4:4 · Enoch taken, Genesis 5:24 · Noah obeys, Genesis 6:22

title: By faith Moses chose to be mistreated with the people of God rather than enjoy the passing pleasure of sin.
paragraphs: By faith Moses, when grown, refused to be called a son of Pharaoh’s daughter, choosing rather to be mistreated with the people of God than to have the temporary enjoyment of sin. He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking toward the reward. By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger, for he endured as though seeing the invisible One.
Scripture and event: Moses leaves Pharaoh’s house, Exodus 2:11–15

paragraphs: And likewise was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works, when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another way? For just as the body without spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.

title: The holy women who hoped in God: Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord.
paragraphs: Let your adornment not be the outward kind—braiding hair, putting on gold ornaments, or dressing in garments— but the hidden person of the heart, in the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious before God. For this is how the holy women of former times, who hoped in God, also adorned themselves, submitting themselves to their own husbands, as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord. You have become her children if you do good and do not fear any terror.
Scripture and event: Sarah’s word, Genesis 18:12

title: You have heard of the endurance of Job, and have seen the Lord’s purpose.
paragraphs: Brothers, take as an example of suffering and patience the prophets who spoke in the Lord’s name. Look, we call those who endured blessed. You heard of Job’s endurance and saw the outcome from the Lord, because the Lord is full of compassion and merciful.
Scripture and event: Job blesses the Lord in loss, Job 1:20–22

title: Elijah was a man like us, and he prayed that it might not rain.
paragraphs: Elijah was a human being with experiences like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain; and it did not rain upon the earth for three years and six months. And he prayed again, and heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
Scripture and event: The drought announced, 1 Kings 17:1 · Rain returns, 1 Kings 18:41–45

title: Through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin; Adam is a type of the One to come.
category: Adam, the Promise and the Law
paragraphs: For this reason, just as through one person sin entered the world, and through sin, death, and so death passed to all people, because all sinned— for until law, sin was in the world, but sin is not charged to account when there is no law; nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the likeness of Adam’s transgression, who is a type of the One to come. But the gift is not like the trespass. For if by the one man’s trespass the many died, much more did God’s grace and the gift in the grace of the one Man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many.
Also taught in: 1 Corinthians 15:21–22 · 1 Corinthians 15:45–49 Scripture and event: The fall, Genesis 3:17–19 · Man made a living soul, Genesis 2:7

title: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his offspring; the Law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, was our guardian until Christ.
category: Adam, the Promise and the Law
paragraphs: Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say, “And to seeds,” as concerning many, but as concerning one, “And to your seed,” who is Christ. What I mean is this: the law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to nullify the promise. For if the inheritance is from law, it is no longer from promise. But God has graciously given it to Abraham through promise. Why, then, the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom the promise had been made, and it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator. … So the law became our guardian until Christ, so that we might be justified by faith. But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
Scripture and event: The promise to Abraham’s offspring, Genesis 12:7 · Four hundred and thirty years, Exodus 12:40

title: Hagar and Sarah are two covenants: the child of the slave and the child of the free woman.
category: Adam, the Promise and the Law
paragraphs: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and one by the free woman. But the one by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, and the one by the free woman through promise. These things are being interpreted allegorically, for these women are two covenants: one from Mount Sinai, bearing children into slavery, which is Hagar. Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is enslaved with her children. But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother. … But what does Scripture say? “Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall certainly not inherit with the son of the free woman.” Therefore, brothers, we are not children of a slave woman but of the free woman.
Scripture and event: Ishmael born, Genesis 16:15 · Isaac born, Genesis 21:2 · Cast out the slave woman, Genesis 21:10

title: Circumcision is of the heart, in spirit and not in letter.
category: Adam, the Promise and the Law
paragraphs: For the Jew is not the one outwardly so, nor is circumcision what is outward in flesh; but the Jew is the one inwardly so, and circumcision is of the heart, in Spirit, not in letter, whose praise is not from people but from God.

title: You shall not muzzle an ox while it threshes: it was written for our sake, that the worker should share the crop.
category: Adam, the Promise and the Law
paragraphs: Am I saying these things merely in a human way, or does not the law also say them? For in the law of Moses it is written, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it threshes.” Is it oxen that concern God, or does He surely say it for our sake? For it was written for our sake, because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the thresher in hope of sharing. If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it a great matter if we reap your material things?
Also taught in: 1 Timothy 5:18 Scripture and event: The ox that threshes, Deuteronomy 25:4

verses.text: Am I saying these things merely in a human way, or does not the law also say them? For in the law of Moses it is written, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it threshes.” Is it oxen that concern God, or does He surely say it for our sake? For it was written for our sake, because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the thresher in hope of sharing. If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it a great matter if we reap your material things?

title: That there may be equality: the one who gathered much had nothing over.
category: Adam, the Promise and the Law
paragraphs: For it is not that there should be relief for others and affliction for you, but on the basis of equality: at the present time your abundance is for their lack, so that their abundance may also be for your lack, so that there may be equality. As it is written, “The one with much had no excess, and the one with little had no shortage.”
Scripture and event: The measure of manna, Exodus 16:18

title: Whoever keeps the whole Law but stumbles in one point has become guilty of all.
category: Adam, the Promise and the Law
paragraphs: For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point has become accountable for all of it. For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law. So speak and so act as those who are going to be judged through a law of freedom.
Scripture and event: The commandments, Exodus 20:13–15

title: The days are coming when I will make a new covenant, and will write My laws upon their hearts.
category: Adam, the Promise and the Law
paragraphs: For, finding fault with them, He says, “Look, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will conclude a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah, not according to the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took hold of their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord. For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws into their mind, I will also inscribe them upon their hearts, and I will be their God, and they will be My people. And they shall certainly not teach, each his fellow citizen and each his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because all will know Me, from their small to their great. …
Also taught in: Hebrews 10:15–17 · 2 Corinthians 3:5–6 Scripture and event: The new covenant foretold, Jeremiah 38:31–34

title: These things happened as examples for us: not to be idolaters, not to commit sexual immorality, not to test Christ, not to grumble.
paragraphs: For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea, and all underwent baptism into Moses in the cloud and in the sea, and all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ. But God was not pleased with most of them, for they were strewn over the wilderness. Now these things became examples for us, so that we might not desire evil things as they also desired. Do not become idolaters, as some of them did, just as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose to play.” Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day. …
Scripture and event: The golden calf, Exodus 32:6 · Baal of Peor, Numbers 25:1–9 · The serpents, Numbers 21:5–6 · The grumbling after Korah, Numbers 17:6–14

title: Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts; a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God.
paragraphs: Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness, where your fathers tested Me with a trial and saw My works for forty years. Therefore I was indignant with this generation and said, ‘They always wander in their heart, and they did not know My ways,’ as I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall certainly not enter My rest.’” Watch out, brothers, lest there be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another each day, as long as it is called “Today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceit of sin. … So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God. For the one who entered His rest also himself rested from his works, just as God did from His own. Therefore let us be diligent to enter that rest, so that no one may fall in the same pattern of disobedience.
Scripture and event: Do not harden your hearts, Psalm 94 (95):7–11 · God rested on the seventh day, Genesis 2:2 · The oath in the wilderness, Numbers 14:22–23

title: See that no one is immoral or profane like Esau, who for one meal gave up his birthright.
paragraphs: Pursue peace with everyone, and sanctification, without which no one will see the Lord. Watch lest anyone fall short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness grow up and cause trouble, and through it many be defiled, lest anyone be sexually immoral or profane like Esau, who sold his own birthright for a single meal. For you know that even afterward, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for repentance, although he sought it with tears.
Scripture and event: Esau sells his birthright, Genesis 25:29–34

title: Moses put a veil over his face; when one turns to the Lord the veil is taken away.
paragraphs: Therefore, having such hope, we use great boldness, and are not like Moses, who put a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel might not gaze at the end of what was being brought to an end. But their minds were hardened. For until this very day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant, not being unveiled, because in Christ it is brought to an end. But to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart. But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is removed. Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. And we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as from the Lord, the Spirit.
Scripture and event: The veil of Moses, Exodus 34:33–35

title: The Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands: Heaven is My throne.
paragraphs: Our fathers had the Tent of Testimony in the wilderness, as the One who spoke to Moses directed him to make it according to the pattern he had seen. Our fathers in their turn received it and brought it in with Joshua when they took possession of the nations’ land, whose people God drove out before our fathers. It remained until the days of David, who found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling for the God of Jacob. But Solomon built Him a house. Yet the Most High does not dwell in things made by hands, as the prophet says: ‘Heaven is My throne, and the earth the footstool of My feet. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or what place is there for My rest? Did not My hand make all these things?’
Also taught in: Acts 17:24–25 Scripture and event: Heaven is My throne, Isaiah 66:1–2

title: Christ our Passover has been sacrificed; let us keep the feast with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
category: Christ in the Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump of dough? Clean out the old leaven so that you may be a new lump of dough, just as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed. So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
Scripture and event: The Passover lamb slain, Exodus 12:21 · Leaven removed, Exodus 12:15

title: A priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
category: Christ in the Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him. Abraham also apportioned to him a tenth of everything. His name is interpreted first as king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace. Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither a beginning of days nor an end of life, but made like the Son of God, he remains a priest continually. … And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek, who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life. For it is testified, “You are a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
Also taught in: Hebrews 5:5–6 Scripture and event: Melchizedek blesses Abraham, Genesis 14:18–20 · The oath of the Lord, Psalm 109 (110):4

title: Christ entered once for all into the holy places, not with the blood of goats and calves but with His own blood.
category: Christ in the Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship. But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance. … But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation— and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption. For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!
Scripture and event: The Day of Atonement, Leviticus 16:15–16 · Once a year, Leviticus 16:34 · The red heifer, Numbers 19:2–9

title: It is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins: a body You prepared for Me.
category: Christ in the Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins. Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me. In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin You took no pleasure. Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Your will, O God.’” After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin You did not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law— He then said, “Look, I have come to do Your will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second. By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
Scripture and event: Sacrifice You did not desire, Psalm 39 (40):7–9

title: Jesus suffered outside the gate; let us go out to Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach.
category: Christ in the Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: We have an altar from which those serving the tent have no authority to eat. For the bodies of those animals whose blood the high priest brings into the holy places for sin are burned outside the camp. Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the gate, so that He might sanctify the people through His own blood. So let us go out to Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach. For here we have no lasting city, but we seek the one to come.
Scripture and event: Burned outside the camp, Leviticus 16:27

title: The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.
category: Christ in the Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: For it stands in Scripture: “Look, I am laying in Zion a stone, a chosen, precious cornerstone, and the one who believes in Him will certainly not be put to shame.” Therefore, the honor is for you who believe; but for those who do not believe, “The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner,” and “a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble, disobeying the word; to this they were also appointed.

title: David, being a prophet, foresaw and spoke of the resurrection of the Christ.
category: Christ in the Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: For David says concerning Him, ‘I kept the Lord before me always, for He is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken. Therefore my heart rejoiced and my tongue exulted; moreover, my flesh will dwell in hope, because You will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor allow Your Holy One to see decay. You have made known to me the paths of life; You will fill me with gladness in Your presence.’ Men, brothers, I may speak openly to you about the patriarch David: he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day. Since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn an oath to him to seat one of his descendants upon his throne, he foresaw and spoke about the resurrection of the Christ: He was neither abandoned to Hades, nor did His flesh see decay. …

category: Christ in the Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: Therefore, exalted to God’s right hand and having received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit, He has poured out this which you see and hear. For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself says, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”’ Therefore let the whole house of Israel know with certainty that God has made Him both Lord and Christ—this Jesus whom you crucified.”

title: The council at Jerusalem: not to trouble the nations who turn to God, but to abstain from things polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from what is strangled, and from blood.
category: Christ in the Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: After they fell silent, James spoke: “Men, brothers, listen to me. Simeon has related how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for His name. With this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written: ‘After these things I will return and rebuild David’s fallen tent. I will rebuild its ruins and set it upright, so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, and all the nations upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things known from long ago.’ Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from the Gentiles who are turning to God, but should write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, sexual immorality, what is strangled, and blood. … For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no further burden upon you except these necessary things: to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, blood, things strangled, and sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.”

title: We were eyewitnesses of His majesty when the voice came: This is My beloved Son.
category: Christ in the Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: For we did not follow cleverly devised myths when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we became eyewitnesses of His majesty. title: Whom the Lord loves He disciplines; endure it as sons.
category: Wisdom for the Household of God
paragraphs: and you have forgotten the encouragement that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline, nor faint when reproved by Him. For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and scourges every son He receives.” Endure for discipline. God deals with you as sons; for what son is there whom a father does not discipline? But if you are without discipline, in which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate children and not sons. Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh as disciplinarians and respected them. Shall we not much more submit to the Father of spirits and live? For they disciplined us for a few days according to what seemed right to them, but He for our benefit, so that we may share in His holiness. …

title: Adam was formed first, then Eve: the apostle’s order for teaching in the assembly.

But she will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and sanctification with self-restraint.

title: The Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: The Lord does not loosen the Law. He gathers it into two commandments and says that everything else hangs on them. The wisdom books call the commandment a lamp, the psalmist loves it, and the prophets ask what the Lord seeks from a human being.

Do not suppose that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to abolish but to fulfill. For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke will pass from the Law until everything happens. Therefore, whoever loosens one of these least commandments and teaches people accordingly will be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of the heavens. For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of the heavens.

Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one. You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole mind, and with your whole strength.’

Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law. For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” Love does not work evil toward the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.
The Householder’s Treasure. Every scribe trained for the kingdom brings out of his treasure things new and old.

Son, do not forget my ordinances; let your heart keep my words, for they will add length of life, years of living, and peace to you. Do not let acts of mercy and faithfulness fail you. Fasten them around your neck, and you will find favor. And take thought for good things before the Lord and people.
because the commandment of law is a lamp and a light, and correction and discipline are life’s way,
One who turns his ear aside so as not to hear the law has himself also abhorred his own prayer.

The Lord’s law is blameless, turning souls; the Lord’s testimony is trustworthy, making infants wise. The Lord’s ordinances are upright, rejoicing the heart; the Lord’s commandment shines afar, giving light to the eyes.
How I loved Your law, Lord! It is my meditation all day.

Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, and did not stand in the way of sinners, and did not sit in the seat of pestilent people; but his will is in the Lord’s law, and on His law he will meditate day and night.

title: You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You
category: You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You
paragraphs: Six times He says, You heard that it was said, but I tell you, and each time He carries the commandment from the hand to the heart: from murder to anger, from adultery to the look, from the oath to the plain word, from repayment to love of the enemy. Proverbs had already told Israel to feed an enemy and to leave repayment to the Lord.

You heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘You shall not murder,’ and ‘Whoever murders will be liable to judgment.’ But I tell you that everyone angry with his brother will be liable to judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool,’ will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.

You heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I tell you: love your enemies and pray for those persecuting you, so that you may become sons of your Father in the heavens, because He makes His sun rise upon evil and good people and sends rain upon righteous and unrighteous people. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You, therefore, shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.
Nathan: The Poor Man’s Ewe Lamb. The rich man takes the poor man’s one lamb; David condemns him, and Nathan answers, You are the man.
Anger destroys even intelligent people; but a yielding answer turns away wrath, and a painful word raises angers.
Do not let desire for beauty overcome you; do not be hunted by your own eyes, nor seized by her eyelids.
If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord will repay you good things.
Do not say, “I will punish the enemy.” But wait for the Lord, so that He may help you.
Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but one who performs faithful deeds is acceptable to Him.
Cease from anger and abandon wrath; do not be provoked to envy so as to act wickedly.
Be angry, and do not sin; speak in your hearts, and upon your beds be pierced with remorse. Diapsalma.

One who walks blamelessly and works righteousness, speaking truth in his heart, who did not act deceitfully with his tongue, nor do evil to his neighbor, and did not take up reproach against those nearest him. One who acts wickedly is held in contempt before him, but he honors those who fear the Lord; one who swears to his neighbor and does not set it aside.

title: Marriage
paragraphs: Asked about divorce, He goes behind the permission of Moses to the beginning: the two become one flesh, and what God has yoked together no one is to separate. Proverbs says the same in its own way: a wife is joined to a husband by God.

He answered, “Have you not read that the Creator from the beginning made them male and female, and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’? So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has yoked together, let no human being separate.” They said to Him, “Why then did Moses command giving a certificate of divorce and divorcing her?” He said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart Moses permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so. I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery; and the one who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”

To the married I give this instruction—not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband— but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and a husband is not to dismiss his wife.
The Foundling Bride. The Lord finds Jerusalem cast out at birth, raises and adorns her, and she turns to prostitution; yet He will remember His covenant.

Let your fountain of water be your own, and share joy with the wife of your youth. Let a deer of affection and a colt of your graces keep company with you. Let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time, for as you move in the company of her affection, you will be one among many.
One who found a good wife found favors, and received gladness from God.
Fathers apportion house and property to children, but a wife is joined to a husband by God.

A courageous woman—who will find her? Such a woman is more precious than costly stones. Her husband’s heart is confident in her; such a woman will not lack fine spoils. For she works good things for her husband throughout her life.
Your wife is like a flourishing vine in the sides of your house; your sons are like newly planted olive trees around your table.
