I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery; and the one who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”

To the married I give this instruction—not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband— but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and a husband is not to dismiss his wife.

Let your fountain of water be your own, and share joy with the wife of your youth. Let a deer of affection and a colt of your graces keep company with you. Let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time, for as you move in the company of her affection, you will be one among many.
One who found a good wife found favors, and received gladness from God.
Fathers apportion house and property to children, but a wife is joined to a husband by God.

A courageous woman—who will find her? Such a woman is more precious than costly stones. Her husband’s heart is confident in her; such a woman will not lack fine spoils. For she works good things for her husband throughout her life.
Your wife is like a flourishing vine in the sides of your house; your sons are like newly planted olive trees around your table.

title: The Sabbath
paragraphs: The Sabbath was made for man. He answers the charge from David and the holy loaves, from the rest the Law gives even to the slave and the ox, and from Hosea: mercy and not sacrifice. The righteous, says Proverbs, has compassion even on his animals.

He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him: how he entered God’s house in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of presentation, which only priests may lawfully eat, and also gave them to those who were with him?” He said to them, “The Sabbath came into being for humankind, and not humankind for the Sabbath. So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”

Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness, where your fathers tested Me with a trial and saw My works for forty years. Therefore I was indignant with this generation and said, ‘They always wander in their heart, and they did not know My ways,’ as I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall certainly not enter My rest.’” Watch out, brothers, lest there be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another each day, as long as it is called “Today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceit of sin. … So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God. For the one who entered His rest also himself rested from his works, just as God did from His own. Therefore let us be diligent to enter that rest, so that no one may fall in the same pattern of disobedience.
The righteous has compassion on the lives of his animals, but the inward affections of the impious are merciless.
Do not refrain from doing good to someone in need whenever your hand has the means to help.
It is good to give thanks to the Lord and make music to Your name, Most High, to declare Your mercy in the morning and Your truth by night,

For He is our God, and we are the people of His pasture and the sheep of His hand. Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness,

title: Clean and Unclean, and the Tradition of the Elders
category: Clean and Unclean, and the Tradition of the Elders
paragraphs: Nothing from outside defiles; what comes out of the heart defiles. The Law’s care for clean and unclean is carried inward, where Proverbs had already set the guard and David had asked for a clean heart.

Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand. There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.” When He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable. He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him, because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods. He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person. For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders, adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness. All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”

I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; except that to the one who reckons something unclean, to that person it is unclean. … For God’s kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit;
With every guard keep your heart, for from these come life’s outlets.
Who will boast that he has a pure heart? Or who will speak confidently of being clean from sins?
Evil offspring judge themselves righteous, but have not washed away their discharge.
Create a clean heart in me, God, and renew an upright spirit in my inward parts.

Who will ascend the Lord’s mountain, and who will stand in His holy place? One innocent in hands and pure in heart, who did not take up his soul for emptiness and did not swear deceitfully to his neighbor.

title: The Commandments and the One Thing Lacking
category: The Commandments and the One Thing Lacking
paragraphs: To the one who asks how to enter life He first gives the commandments, and then the one thing lacking: sell, give, and follow. The psalms and proverbs agree that wealth does not go down with its owner, and that the law of God’s mouth is better than thousands of gold and silver.

He said to him, “Why do you ask Me about what is good? One is good. But if you wish to enter life, keep the commandments.” He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; honor father and mother’; and ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”
Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “You lack one thing. Go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law. For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” Love does not work evil toward the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.
The Hidden Treasure. A man sells all that he has, for joy, to buy the field where the treasure lies.
The Pearl of Great Price. A merchant sells everything to buy one pearl of great value.
One who trusts in wealth will fall, but one who supports righteous people will spring up.
Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, and offer Him firstfruits from your fruits of righteousness,
Better a small portion with the fear of the Lord than great storehouses with fearlessness.
Do not fear when a person grows rich and when the glory of his house increases. For when he dies he will not take everything, nor will his glory descend with him.
The law of Your mouth is better for me than thousands of gold and silver.

title: Temple, Offerings and Tithes
paragraphs: He honors the temple, sends the leper to the priest, and pays the tax; and He says with the prophets that God desires mercy and not sacrifice, and that His house is a house of prayer for all the nations. David had said it first: a sacrifice to God is a broken spirit.
Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call righteous people, but sinners.”
He taught and said to them, “Is it not written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”

Therefore I urge you, brothers, through God’s mercies, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, your rational worship. And do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of the mind, so that you may discern what God’s will is: the good and pleasing and perfect.
Doing righteous things and speaking truth are more pleasing before God than the blood of sacrifices.
The sacrifices of the impious are an abomination to the Lord, but the prayers of those going straight are acceptable to Him.
The sacrifices of the impious are an abomination to the Lord, for they offer them lawlessly.
For if You had desired sacrifice, I would have given it; You will not delight in burnt offerings. A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise.
Will I eat bulls’ flesh or drink goats’ blood? Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God and pay your vows to the Most High.
for zeal for Your house devoured me, and the reproaches of those reproaching You fell upon me.
For one day in Your courts is better than thousands; I chose to be cast aside in the house of God rather than dwell in the tents of sinners.

title: Done to Be Seen
paragraphs: What is done to be seen has its reward already. He sets the scribes’ long fringes beside a widow’s two small coins. Proverbs: let your neighbor praise you, and not your own mouth.

He called His disciples to Him and said to them, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all those putting into the treasury. For they all put in from their surplus, but she, from her need, put in everything she had—her whole livelihood.”
The Pharisee and the Tax Collector. The one who humbled himself went down to his house justified rather than the other.
The Lowest Place at the Feast. Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.
Let your neighbor praise you, and not your mouth, another, and not your lips.
Everyone high of heart is unclean before God, and one who unjustly puts hands into a hand will not be acquitted.

Do not boast before a king, and do not station yourself in the places of rulers; for it is better for you to be told, “Come up to me,” than for him to humble you before a ruler. Say what your eyes have seen.
Each spoke empty things to his neighbor; deceitful lips spoke with a heart and a heart. May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and a boastful tongue—
Lord, my heart was not exalted, nor were my eyes raised high; I did not walk among great things nor among wonders beyond me.

title: Repent and Believe
paragraphs: His first word is Repent, and it is the word of every prophet before Him: turn back and live. With it comes faith, new birth, the child’s lowliness, and the narrow gate, which Proverbs knows as the way that only seems upright and the way that shines.
From then on Jesus began to proclaim, “Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.”

Enter through the narrow gate, because the gate is wide and the road broad that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. Because the gate is narrow and the road constricted that leads to life, and few find it.

Peter said to them, “Repent, and let each one of you be baptized upon the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is for you, for your children, and for all who are far away—as many as the Lord our God calls to Himself.”
The Lost Son. The father runs to the son who was dead and is alive again, and pleads with the elder brother.
The Lost Sheep. There is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
The Lost Coin. There is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.
The Two Sons. The one who said No but went did the father’s will: tax collectors and prostitutes go into the kingdom before you.
The Barren Fig Tree. Leave it this year also, until I dig around it and put on manure.

Trust God with your whole heart; do not exalt yourself on the strength of your wisdom. In all your ways acknowledge her, so that she may cut your ways straight, and your foot will certainly not stumble.
But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go forward and illuminate until the day comes right. But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble.
There is a way that seems upright to people, but its final outcome comes to the bottom of Hades.

Have mercy on me, God, according to Your great mercy, and according to the abundance of Your compassion blot out my lawless deed. Wash me more and more from my lawlessness, and cleanse me from my sin. For I know my lawlessness, and my sin is continually before me.
Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will certainly not reckon, and in whose mouth there is no deceit.
I made my sin known, and I did not cover my lawlessness. I said, “I will confess my lawlessness against myself to the Lord,” and You forgave the impiety of my sin. Diapsalma.
If I was not humble-minded, but exalted my soul— like the weaned child upon its mother, like repayment upon my soul.

title: Follow Me
paragraphs: Follow Me: the call that took Abram from his land and Elisha from the plow. It costs everything and it gives rest. Wisdom asks the same of her sons: give me your heart, and do not turn to the right or to the left.

Then Jesus said to His disciples, “If anyone wishes to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life because of Me will find it.

Come to Me, all who toil and are burdened, and I will give you rest. Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, because I am meek and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For My yoke is kind, and My burden is light.”

Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death? Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the Father’s glory, so we also might walk in newness of life.
The Tower Builder and the King Going to War. Whoever would be His disciple must first sit down and count the cost.
The Hidden Treasure. A man sells all that he has, for joy, to buy the field where the treasure lies.
The Pearl of Great Price. A merchant sells everything to buy one pearl of great value.
The Grain of Wheat. Unless it falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
Give me your heart, son, and let your eyes keep my ways;

Let your eyes look straight, and let your eyelids incline toward righteous things. Make straight tracks for your feet and direct your ways aright. Do not turn to the right or the left; turn your foot away from an evil way.

Blessed is the person who found wisdom, the mortal who saw good sense, for trading in her is better than treasures of gold and silver. She is more valuable than costly stones; nothing evil will stand against her. She is readily known to all who approach her, and nothing precious is worthy of her.

The Lord shepherds me, and nothing will fail me. He made me dwell in a place of green growth; He nourished me beside water of rest. He turned my soul back; He guided me upon paths of righteousness for His name’s sake. For even if I walk in the midst of death’s shadow, I will fear no evils, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff comforted me.
My soul clung behind You; Your right hand supported me.
For what is there for me in heaven? And what did I desire from You upon the earth? My heart and my flesh failed; the God of my heart and my portion is God forever.
I kept seeing the Lord before me continually, because He is at my right hand, so that I may not be shaken.

title: Hear and Keep
paragraphs: To hear and not to do is to build on sand. Israel said at Sinai, We will do and obey; Ezekiel’s hearers listened as to a sweet song and did nothing. The one who keeps the word is the tree by the waters that gives its fruit in its season, the branch that remains in the vine.

Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and does them will be likened to a prudent man who built his house upon the rock. The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and fell upon that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock. And everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not do them will be likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand. The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell; and its fall was great.”
“If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.

And by this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments. The one who says, “I have come to know Him,” and does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in that person. But whoever keeps His word, in that person the love of God has truly been brought to completion. By this we know that we are in Him. The one who says that he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked.
The Two Builders. Whoever hears His words and does them builds on rock; whoever hears and does not, on sand.
The Sower. The seed is the word; the four soils are four ways of hearing it. The Lord explains it Himself.
The True Vine. He is the true vine, His Father the vinegrower, the disciples the branches.
The Lamp on the Lampstand. A lamp is not lit to be hidden; nothing is hidden except to be revealed.

Isaiah: The Song of the Vineyard. The beloved did everything for his vineyard and it yielded thorns; the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel. The Lord’s parable of the tenants takes up this song.
When a storm passes by, the impious disappears, but the righteous turns aside and is saved forever.

Son, guard my words, and hide my commandments with yourself. Son, honor the Lord and you will be strong; apart from Him, fear no other. Guard my commandments and you will live, and my words like the pupils of eyes. Put them around your fingers; inscribe them on the broad surface of your heart.
One who keeps a command guards his own life, but one who despises his own ways will perish.
But whoever listens to me will dwell in hope and rest fearlessly from every evil.
In my heart I hid Your sayings, so that I might not sin against You.

but his will is in the Lord’s law, and on His law he will meditate day and night. He will be like the tree planted beside the outlets of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and whose leaf will not fall off; and everything he does will be prospered.

I considered Your ways and turned my feet toward Your testimonies. I was prepared and was not troubled to keep Your commandments.

title: The New Commandment
paragraphs: The new commandment is the old one given a measure: as I have loved you. Its ground is the name the Lord proclaimed to Moses, compassionate and merciful, and its reach is the newcomer and the enemy.

I give you a new commandment, that you love one another. Just as I loved you, you also are to love one another. By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you have love among one another.”
Become merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
In everything I showed you that by working in this way we must support the weak and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
The Good Samaritan. The neighbor is the one who showed mercy. Go, and do likewise.
The Two Debtors. The one who is forgiven much loves much.
Hatred raises strife, but friendship covers all who do not love strife.
Let a friend be yours at every time, and let brothers be useful in necessities; for this is why they are born.
Do not let acts of mercy and faithfulness fail you. Fasten them around your neck, and you will find favor.
One who dishonors the needy sins, but one who has mercy on the poor is blessed.
Look, what is good or what is delightful except for brothers to dwell together?
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy.
As a father has compassion on children, the Lord had compassion on those who fear Him,

title: Judging and Forgiving
paragraphs: Judge not; forgive; and if your brother sins, go to him. Lamech boasted of vengeance seventy times seven, and the Lord turns the number into forgiveness. The psalmist knows why: if You closely watch lawless deeds, Lord, who will withstand?

Do not judge, so that you may not be judged. For with the judgment you use, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you. Why do you see the splinter in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the beam in your own eye? Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Let me remove the splinter from your eye,’ when behold, the beam is in your own eye? Hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the splinter from your brother’s eye.

Then Peter came and said to Him, “Lord, how often will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?” Jesus said to him, “I do not tell you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.

Therefore put on, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, tender compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience, bearing with one another and forgiving one another if anyone has a complaint against someone. Just as the Lord forgave you, so also must you.
The Unforgiving Slave. The one forgiven ten thousand talents would not forgive a hundred denarii: so My heavenly Father will do to you, unless each of you forgives his brother from the heart.
The Lost Son. The father runs to the son who was dead and is alive again, and pleads with the elder brother.
The Pharisee and the Tax Collector. The one who humbled himself went down to his house justified rather than the other.
Nathan: The Poor Man’s Ewe Lamb. The rich man takes the poor man’s one lamb; David condemns him, and Nathan answers, You are the man.
If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and at his tripping do not lift yourself up, for the Lord will see, and it will not please Him, and He will turn His wrath away from him.
Do not reprove evil people, so that they may not hate you; reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
Open rebukes are better than concealed friendship. A friend’s wounds are more trustworthy than an enemy’s willing kisses.
One who hides wrongdoings seeks friendship, but one who hates hiding them separates friends and household members.
If You closely watch lawless deeds, Lord, Lord, who will withstand? For with You is atonement.

He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our lawless deeds, for according to heaven’s height above the earth, the Lord strengthened His mercy toward those who fear Him. As far as the east is distant from the west, He removed our lawless deeds from us.
A righteous man will discipline me in mercy and correct me, but let a sinner’s oil not enrich my head, for still my prayer is amid their good pleasures.

title: Serving
paragraphs: The great one is the servant, as the Son of Man came to serve: the Servant of Isaiah, and the king of Zechariah who comes gentle. The whole of Scripture stands behind His word that the one who exalts himself will be humbled.

It shall not be so among you. Instead, whoever wishes to become great among you will be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you will be your slave, just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give His life as a ransom in place of many.”
So if I, the Lord and the Teacher, washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, so that you also may do just as I did to you.

doing nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility considering one another above yourselves, each looking not to your own interests, but each also to those of others. Have this mind among yourselves which was also in Christ Jesus, who, existing in the form of God, did not regard being equal with God as something to exploit, but emptied Himself, taking the form of a slave, coming to be in the likeness of human beings; and being found in appearance as a human being, He humbled Himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross.
The Unprofitable Slaves. When you have done all that was commanded, say, We have done what we ought to have done.
The Lowest Place at the Feast. Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.
The Watchful Slaves. Blessed are those slaves whom the master finds awake: he will gird himself and serve them.
Insolence leads before ruin, and evil-mindedness before a fall. Better a gentle-tempered person with humility than one who divides spoils with the insolent.
Insolence brings a man low, but the Lord supports the humble-minded with glory.
Wherever insolence enters, dishonor is there too, but the mouth of the humble meditates on wisdom.
The Lord opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
For the Lord is high and watches the lowly, and the lofty He knows from afar.

Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells in high places, and looks upon lowly things in heaven and on earth? He raises the poor from the ground and lifts the needy from the dung heap, to seat him with rulers, with the rulers of His people.
He will guide the meek in judgment; He will teach the meek His ways.

title: The Little Ones and the Poor
category: The Little Ones and the Poor
paragraphs: What is done to the least is done to Him. Proverbs had said it of the Maker: whoever has mercy on the poor lends to God, and whoever extorts from the needy provokes the One who made him.
When Jesus saw it, He was indignant and said to them, “Let the children come to Me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.’

But whoever has this world’s means of living and sees his brother in need and closes his heart against him, how does the love of God abide in him? Little children, let us not love in word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
The Sheep and the Goats. Insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.
The Great Supper. Those first invited made excuses; the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame are brought in.
The Rich Man and Lazarus. If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead.
The Lost Sheep. There is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
One who extorts from the needy provokes the One who made him, but one who honors Him has mercy on the poor.
One who has mercy on the poor lends to God, and He will repay him according to his gift.
One who blocks his ears from hearing the weak will himself also call, and there will be no one listening.
One who has mercy on the poor will himself be nourished, for he gave of his own loaves to the poor.
Open your mouth for God’s word, and judge everyone soundly. Open your mouth and judge justly, and decide the case of the poor and weak.
Blessed is the one who understands the poor and needy; in an evil day the Lord will rescue him.
From the mouth of infants and nursing children You prepared praise, because of Your enemies, to bring down the enemy and the avenger.
Judge for the fatherless and the poor; vindicate the lowly and the needy. Deliver the needy and the poor; rescue them from the hand of a sinner.”
the Father of orphans and judge of widows, God in His holy place.

title: In Secret
paragraphs: Alms, prayer and fasting are for the Father who sees in secret. Elisha shut the door and prayed; Daniel went to his upper room; the prophets of Baal called from morning until noon. The psalmist already knows the One who sees: You knew my sitting and my rising.

And when you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites, because they love to pray standing in synagogues and at street corners, so that people may see them. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full. But you, when you pray, enter your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you. When praying, do not babble like the Gentiles, for they think they will be heard through their many words. So do not become like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.

Now this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows in blessings will also reap in blessings. Let each give as he has decided in his heart, not out of sorrow or compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
The Pharisee and the Tax Collector. The one who humbled himself went down to his house justified rather than the other.
There are those who sow their own things and produce more, and there are those who gather and become diminished.
One who gives to the poor will not be in need; but one who turns away his eye will be in great difficulty.
God is far distant from the impious, but He listens to the prayers of the righteous.
Lord, You tested me and knew me. You knew my sitting and my rising; You understood my reasonings from afar. You traced my path and my measuring cord, and You foresaw all my ways.
Let my prayer be directed as incense before You, the lifting of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
But when they troubled me, I put on sackcloth and humbled my soul with fasting; and my prayer will return to my bosom.

title: Pray in This Way
paragraphs: The prayer He gave gathers the prayers of Israel: the Father of Isaiah, the great Name that Ezekiel heard would be sanctified, the bread of each day from the wilderness and from Proverbs, the guard against the evil day from the Psalms. And He commands the asking itself: seek, and you will find.

You, then, pray like this: ‘Our Father in the heavens, let Your name be hallowed. Let Your kingdom come. Let Your will be done, as in heaven, also upon earth. Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And do not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from evil.’
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Rejoice always. Pray unceasingly. Give thanks in everything, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.
The Friend at Midnight. Because of his persistence he will rise and give him whatever he needs.
The Widow and the Unjust Judge. Will not God bring about justice for His chosen ones who cry to Him day and night?

Put a vain and false word far from me; give me neither wealth nor poverty; assign me what is needed and sufficient, so that I may not become full and false and say, ‘Who sees me?’ or become poor and steal and swear by the name of God.

for if you call upon wisdom and give your voice to understanding, and seek perception with a loud voice, and if you seek it like silver and search it out like treasures, then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God. For the Lord gives wisdom, and from His presence come knowledge and understanding.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me.
The Lord is near to all who call on Him, to all who call on Him in truth. He will fulfill the will of those who fear Him; He will hear their plea and save them.
But I cried to God, and the Lord heard me. Evening, morning and noon I will recount; I will proclaim, and He will hear my voice.
My heart said to You, “My face sought You.” Your face, Lord, I will seek.
Call on Me in the day of affliction; I will rescue you, and you will glorify Me.” Diapsalma.

Set a guard, Lord, for my mouth and a restraining door around my lips. Do not turn my heart toward words of wickedness, to offer excuses for sins with people who practice lawlessness, and I will certainly not join with their chosen ones.

title: Treasure
paragraphs: Treasure on earth is kept in a pierced bag, says Haggai; the one who stores it does not know for whom he gathers, says the psalm. The Lord says where to keep it instead, and whose image is on the coin and whose on the man.

Do not store up treasures for yourselves upon earth, where moth and consumption destroy and where thieves break through and steal. But store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor consumption destroys and where thieves neither break through nor steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart will also be.
No one can serve as a slave to two masters: for he will either hate the one and love the other, or hold to one and despise the other. You cannot serve as a slave to God and mammon.

But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, because neither can we carry anything out. But having food and coverings, with these we will be content. But those who want to become rich fall into temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge human beings into ruin and destruction. For the love of money is a root of all evils, and some, reaching for it, wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains.
The Rich Fool. So is the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.
The Shrewd Steward. The sons of this age are more prudent toward their own generation than the sons of light.
The Rich Man and Lazarus. If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead.
Better a small portion with the fear of the Lord than great storehouses with fearlessness.
A good name is more desirable than much wealth, and good favor is above silver and gold. Rich and poor met one another, and the Lord made both.
There are those who make themselves rich while having nothing, and those who humble themselves amid much wealth.
Fear God, son, and the king, and disobey neither of them;
Indeed a person passes through as an image; yet they are troubled in vain. He stores treasure and does not know for whom he will gather it.
Better is a little for the righteous than the great wealth of sinners.
Do not hope in injustice or long for plunder; if wealth flows, do not attach your heart.

title: Trust
paragraphs: Do not be anxious; do not fear. He points to the ravens, which the Psalms and Job had already seen fed by God, and which fed Elijah. Cast your care upon the Lord, and He will nourish you.

Therefore I tell you: do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear. Is life not more than food, and the body more than clothing? Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow or reap or gather into storehouses, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they?

Be anxious about nothing, but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses every understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
The Seed Growing of Itself. The kingdom grows as seed does, night and day, the sower knows not how, until the harvest.
You will not fear an approaching fright or the oncoming assaults of the ungodly, for the Lord will be upon all your ways and support your foot so that you are not shaken.
having feared and felt shame before people, they were tripped up; but one who trusts in the Lord will rejoice. Impiety gives a man a fall; but one who trusts in the Master will be saved.
The Lord will not starve a righteous life, but He will overturn the life of the impious.
In the fear of the Lord is hope of strength, and he leaves a support for his children.
Cast your care upon the Lord, and He will nourish you; He will never give the righteous a shaking.
I was young and indeed have grown old, and I have not seen a righteous person abandoned or his offspring seeking loaves.
By day I will fear, but I will hope in You. In God I will praise my words all day. In God I have hoped; I will not fear. What will flesh do to me?
who gives the cattle their food and to the young ravens who call upon Him.

title: Watchfulness
paragraphs: Stay awake. The prophets stood at their watch, and they warned of prophets who speak from their own heart and of watchmen who love to doze. Wisdom blesses the one who keeps awake at her doors day by day, and the psalmist waits for the Lord from the morning watch until night.
Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour.

Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves. You will recognize them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

Because if you confess Jesus as Lord with your mouth, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved; for with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses for salvation.
The Ten Virgins. Five were prudent and took oil; the bridegroom came, and the door was shut.
The Doorkeeper. Stay awake, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming.
The Watchful Slaves. Blessed are those slaves whom the master finds awake: he will gird himself and serve them.
The Thief in the Night. If the householder had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake.
The Faithful and the Wicked Slave. Blessed is the slave whom his master finds so doing when he comes.
The Talents. To each according to his ability; to everyone who has, more will be given.
The Minas. Do business until I come.
The Budding Fig Tree. When its branch becomes tender, you know that summer is near.
The Weeds among the Wheat. Good seed and darnel, the weed an enemy sowed, grow together until the harvest, when the Son of Man sends His angels to separate them. The Lord explains it Himself.
The Dragnet. The net gathers every kind; at the end of the age the angels separate the evil from the righteous.
The Blind Leading the Blind. Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?

How long do you lie down, sluggard? When will you rise from sleep? You sleep a little, sit a little, doze a little, and clasp your chest with your hands a little; then poverty arrives beside you like an evil traveler, and want like a good runner.
Happy is the man who will listen to me, and the person who will keep my ways, staying awake at my doors day by day, guarding the posts of my entrances.
Do not boast of things for tomorrow, for you do not know what the coming day will bear.
The innocent person believes every word, but the resourceful comes to reconsideration.
Because of Your law I waited for You, Lord; my soul waited for Your word. My soul hoped in the Lord from the morning watch until night; from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord.
Unless the Lord builds a house, those building it have labored in vain. Unless the Lord guards a city, the watchman has kept awake in vain.
My eyes were awake before dawn to meditate on Your sayings.
And I spoke of Your testimonies before kings, and I was not ashamed.

I proclaimed good news of righteousness in a great assembly; look, I will certainly not restrain my lips; Lord, You know. I did not hide Your righteousness in my heart; I spoke of Your truth and Your salvation. I did not hide Your mercy and Your truth from a great congregation.

title: Do This in Remembrance of Me
category: Do This in Remembrance of Me
paragraphs: Do this in remembrance of Me. Behind the Supper stand the Passover kept as a memorial, the blood of the covenant sprinkled at Sinai, the bread from heaven, Melchizedek’s loaves and wine, and Wisdom, who mixed her wine, prepared her table and sent out her servants to call.

And He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body [which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.” And likewise the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, poured out for you.]

For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was being handed over, took bread, and after giving thanks He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.” Likewise He also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of Me.” For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.
The Great Supper. Those first invited made excuses; the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame are brought in.
The Wedding Feast. Many are called, but few are chosen.

Wisdom built herself a house, and set seven pillars beneath it. She slaughtered her own sacrificial animals, mixed her own wine in a mixing-bowl, and prepared her own table. She sent her own servants, summoning with a lofty proclamation to the mixing-bowl, saying: “Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me!” And to those lacking understanding she said: “Come, eat of my loaves, and drink wine that I mixed for you. Leave foolishness, and you will live; seek understanding, so that you may live, and set insight right in knowledge.”
You prepared a table before me opposite those who afflict me; You enriched my head with oil, and Your cup is intoxicating—how excellent!
What shall I repay to the Lord for everything He has repaid to me? I will take the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord.
Taste and see that the Lord is kind; blessed is the man who hopes in Him.
and rained manna for them to eat, and gave them heaven’s bread. A human ate angels’ bread; He sent them food supplies to fullness.
He made remembrance of His wonders; the Lord is merciful and compassionate. He gave food to those who fear Him; He will remember His covenant forever.

title: Go and Make Disciples
paragraphs: All authority has been given to Me: Daniel saw it given to one like a son of man. Go to all the nations: the promise to Abram, the light of Isaiah, the song of the Psalms. And He breathed on them, as God breathed into the first man a breath of life.

Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority in heaven and upon earth has been given to Me. Go, therefore, and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe everything I commanded you. And behold, I am with you all the days until the consummation of the age.”

Peter said to them, “Repent, and let each one of you be baptized upon the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is for you, for your children, and for all who are far away—as many as the Lord our God calls to Himself.”
The Mustard Seed. The smallest of seeds becomes a tree in whose branches the birds make their dwelling.
The Leaven. A little leaven hidden in three measures of flour leavens the whole.
The Dragnet. The net gathers every kind; at the end of the age the angels separate the evil from the righteous.
The Sower. The seed is the word; the four soils are four ways of hearing it. The Lord explains it Himself.
The Seed Growing of Itself. The kingdom grows as seed does, night and day, the sower knows not how, until the harvest.
From the fruit of righteousness a tree of life grows, but the lives of lawless people are taken away before their time.
A faithful witness will rescue a life from evils, but a deceitful person kindles lies.
Rescue those being led to death, and ransom those being killed; do not hold back.
As cold water is welcome to a thirsty life, so is good news from a faraway land.
Sing to the Lord; bless His name. Proclaim the good news of His salvation day after day. Announce His glory among the nations, His wonders among all the peoples.
Their sound went out into all the earth, and their utterances to the limits of the inhabited world. In the sun He set His dwelling.
All the limits of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations will bow down before You, because kingship belongs to the Lord, and He is master of the nations.
Praise the Lord, all nations; laud Him, all peoples,
That Your way may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations.

title: The Sending
paragraphs: He sends them as the prophets were sent: with words put in the mouth, without inheritance, in haste like Gehazi, to be mocked as the messengers were mocked. Those who sow in tears will reap with exultation.
As you go, proclaim, ‘The kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.’ Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Freely you received; freely give.

Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say every evil thing against you because of Me. Rejoice and exult, for your reward is great in the heavens; for in this way they persecuted the prophets before you.
In everything I showed you that by working in this way we must support the weak and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
The Sower. The seed is the word; the four soils are four ways of hearing it. The Lord explains it Himself.
The Workers in the Vineyard. The last receive as the first, for the master is generous; the last will be first and the first last.
The Grain of Wheat. Unless it falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
The Woman in Labor. Her grief turns to joy when the child is born: so your grief will become joy.
An impious person flees when no one pursues, but a righteous person is confident like a lion.
Son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline or lose heart when corrected by Him, for the Lord disciplines the one He loves and scourges every son He receives.
As silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so hearts are chosen before the Lord.
Those sowing in tears will reap with exultation. Going, they went and wept, carrying their seeds; but coming, they will arrive with exultation, carrying their sheaves.
For Your sake we are put to death all day long; we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter.
for on Your account I endured reproach; embarrassment covered my face.
Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and He will rescue them from them all.
The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and my cup; You are the One who restores my inheritance to me.

title: Shepherds of the Flock
paragraphs: Feed My lambs. The charge to Peter answers Moses’ prayer that the congregation not be like sheep without a shepherd, and the long complaint of the prophets against shepherds who fed themselves. Proverbs gives the pastor’s rule in a line: know thoroughly the lives of your flock.

So when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus says to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me more than these?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, You know that I love You.” He says to him, “Feed My lambs.” He says to him again a second time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, You know that I love You.” He says to him, “Shepherd My sheep.” He says to him the third time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” Peter was grieved because He said to him the third time, “Do you love Me?” And he said to Him, “Lord, You know all things; You know that I love You.” Jesus says to him, “Feed My sheep.

Therefore, I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a participant in the glory about to be revealed: Shepherd the flock of God among you, exercising oversight, not under compulsion but willingly, according to God; not for shameful gain but eagerly; not as lording it over those allotted to you, but becoming examples to the flock. And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
The Good Shepherd and the Door. The sheep hear His voice; the good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep. John calls it a figure of speech.
The Lost Sheep. There is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
The Shepherds and the Sheep. Woe to the shepherds who feed themselves; the Lord Himself will seek His sheep. The Lord’s word, I am the good Shepherd, answers this prophecy.
The Faithful and the Wicked Slave. Blessed is the slave whom his master finds so doing when he comes.
Know thoroughly the lives of your flock, and set your heart upon your herds;
Mercy and truth are a guard for a king, and they will surround his throne in righteousness.

And He chose David His servant, and took him up from the flocks of sheep; from behind the ewes giving birth He took him, to shepherd Jacob His people and Israel His inheritance. And he shepherded them in his heart’s innocence, and guided them with his hands’ understanding.
You who shepherd Israel, pay attention, You who guide Joseph like sheep; You who sit upon the cherubim, appear.
Restore to me the exultation of Your salvation, and strengthen me with a governing spirit. I will teach the lawless Your ways, and the ungodly will turn back to You.
Know that the Lord—He is God. He made us, and not we; His people and the sheep of His pasture.

Know thoroughly the lives of your flock, and set your heart upon your herds;
Mercy and truth are a guard for a king, and they will surround his throne in righteousness.

And He chose David His servant, and took him up from the flocks of sheep; from behind the ewes giving birth He took him, to shepherd Jacob His people and Israel His inheritance. And he shepherded them in his heart’s innocence, and guided them with his hands’ understanding.
You who shepherd Israel, pay attention, You who guide Joseph like sheep; You who sit upon the cherubim, appear.
Restore to me the exultation of Your salvation, and strengthen me with a governing spirit. I will teach the lawless Your ways, and the ungodly will turn back to You.
Know that the Lord—He is God. He made us, and not we; His people and the sheep of His pasture.

title: Cross the Jordan with the people
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Joshua 1:2
Original recipient: Joshua and Israel. Record type: Historical commission.
This instruction concerns Joshua’s leadership and Israel’s entry into the land. It does not commission every believer to cross the Jordan or claim territory.

title: Keep and meditate on the law entrusted to Joshua
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Joshua 1:7–9
Original recipient: Joshua. Record type: Historical commission with continuing teaching.
Keep the charge to Joshua and the land promise in context. The passage teaches attentive obedience; its prosperity language is not an unconditional promise of wealth to every reader.

title: Prepare provisions for the crossing
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Joshua 1:10–11
Original recipient: Israel, through Joshua’s officers. Record type: Historical operational direction.
Joshua gives a practical instruction for a particular journey. This is recorded separately from God’s direct commission in verses 2–9.

title: Serve the Lord and remove foreign gods
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Joshua 24:14–24
Original recipient: Israel at the covenant assembly. Record type: Covenant exhortation; continuity review open.

Joshua calls Israel to exclusive allegiance. Read the renewed covenant and the people’s response before applying the passage; this entry is not an additional count of the Torah’s prohibition of idolatry.

title: Trust God without exalting your own wisdom
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Proverbs 3:5–7
Original recipient: The learner addressed as a son. Record type: Wisdom instruction; continuity review open.
The selected Greek-based reading preserves self-exaltation in verse 5 and a feminine pronoun in verse 6. The summary does not replace those details with wording from another edition.

title: Receive the Lord’s discipline
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Proverbs 3:11–12
Original recipient: The learner addressed as a son. Record type: Wisdom instruction; continuity review open.
The instruction concerns responding to God’s correction. Its divine-parent image must not be used as permission for human abuse.

title: Do good promptly when you can help
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Proverbs 3:27–28
Original recipient: The wisdom learner who has means to help. Record type: Wisdom instruction; continuity review open.
The practical condition matters: help when it is within your means. The passage rebukes needless delay in giving available help.

title: Do justice, love mercy and be ready to walk with God
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Micah 6:8
Original recipient: The human hearer within the case against Israel. Record type: Prophetic instruction; continuity review open.
The Saints Greek-based wording says “be ready to walk.” “Humbly” belongs to the comparison tradition and is not silently substituted into this summary.

title: Remember, repent and return to the first works
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Revelation 2:4–7
Original recipient: The addressed church in Ephesus. Record type: Church-directed instruction; wider application requires context.
The call to repentance belongs to Christ’s message concerning abandoned first love. Hear the whole message, including the appeal to the churches in verse 7.
classification: Church-directed instruction; wider application requires context

title: Remain faithful through suffering
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Revelation 2:10–11
Original recipient: The addressed church in Smyrna. Record type: Church-directed instruction; wider application requires context.
Keep the particular warning about coming suffering beside the call to faithfulness. Do not turn the ten days into a universal timetable.
classification: Church-directed instruction; wider application requires context

title: Become watchful, remember and repent
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Revelation 3:2–3
Original recipient: The addressed church in Sardis. Record type: Church-directed instruction; wider application requires context.
Christ’s rebuke concerns the church’s condition and incomplete works. This call is retained with its named audience rather than counted as three new universal laws.
classification: Church-directed instruction; wider application requires context

title: Worship God
paragraphs: Original Scripture: Revelation 22:8–9
Original recipient: John, corrected by the angel. Record type: Direct instruction; continuity review open.
The angel refuses John’s worship and directs him to God. This concerns the object of worship; the messenger’s role does not make the messenger divine.
